clue.text: Clubs are able to sell back drink

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the words just before it in the opposite direction

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to be able is to be able to do it: 'can'
goods that go are sold, as in 'it went for a fiver'

explanation.surface: A bar's card club licensed to sell drink back to its members.
explanation.walkthrough: C stays at the front; only 'are able to sell' is turned round, giving COGNAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a specific kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Warning gold is going down in sale

indicators.note: the chemical symbol for gold already heads the following word and is said to slide further down it, so its letters are reordered

blocks.note: an auction is a sale by bidding; Au, the symbol for gold, already sits at its front

explanation.surface: A shopper's warning that the price of gold is falling at the sales.
explanation.walkthrough: In AUCTION the gold symbol sits at the top; moving AU one place down the word, after the C, gives CAUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A caution is a warning, as in a formal police caution or a word of advice.

clue.text: Acknowledge actor's gift

blocks.note: first meaning: to concede or admit
a third meaning: Cary ... (or Hugh ...), the film actor
second meaning: a sum given

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings in three words: concede, the actor Cary Grant, and money given. The actor ties in with 23 down, LEACH, Cary Grant's original surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to admit it, and a grant is money awarded without repayment, a kind of gift.

clue.text: Doctor cites case of agoraphobic recluse

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the outside letters of agoraphobic

explanation.surface: A doctor quotes a case study of an agoraphobic who shuns company.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone who lives in austere self-denial, often withdrawn from society, so a recluse.

clue.text: Moderate payment in advance expected to arrive

blocks.note: a sub is an advance on wages
a train due at noon is expected then

explanation.surface: Someone moderating their spending while an advance payment is expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective but is the verb: to tone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue is to tone down or restrain, as one moderates a voice or a light.

clue.text: Anxious to be seen as chaste?

blocks.note: first meaning: worried, ill at ease
second, playful meaning: 'easy' is slang for promiscuous, so someone not easy is chaste

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: split the answer as UN-EASY, the opposite of 'easy' in its slang sense of sexually available.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasy means troubled and nervous; read as not-easy it humorously suggests virtue.

clue.text: Novel by me is odd and free from physical constraints

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are made into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author says their own strange novel releases a spirit from the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' sounds like a book the speaker wrote, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To disembody is to separate a soul or spirit from its body, freeing it from physical form.

clue.text: Author audibly expressed regret for destruction of life-support system

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the words are judged by their sound not their spelling

blocks.note: Umberto Eco, Italian author of The Name of the Rose
to sigh is to express regret; 'sighed' said quickly matches the ending

explanation.surface: A writer sighs over the wrecking of a life-support machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eco sighed' spoken aloud is ECOCIDE. The life-support system is the planet's ecosystem, not a hospital machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecocide is wholesale destruction of the natural environment, the system that keeps life going.

clue.text: Green energy company operated illegally retaining six employees regularly at fault

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside, so one piece goes within the company name
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: Enron, the US energy firm that collapsed in 2001 amid accounting fraud
Roman numeral for six
workers, staff
second, fourth and sixth letters of 'at fault'

explanation.surface: A green energy firm ran crooked books while some employees were at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like part of the firm's description but it is the definition. Enron was the US energy giant that collapsed in 2001 amid fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in politics means concerned with protecting the environment, i.e. environmental.

clue.text: Boat with advanced instrument for making deep soundings

blocks.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: A boat carrying sonar equipment to measure the depth of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep soundings' suggests depth measurement from a boat; here it means low musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the lowest-pitched brass instrument, producing deep sounds.

clue.text: Discount Conservative being supported by meeting on record

indicators.note: something on record is captured as sound, so the spoken form counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Con is the short form for a Conservative
a session is a sitting or meeting

explanation.surface: A Tory gets a discount after support at a recorded meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, being supported by just means followed by. 'Con session' spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A concession is a reduced price for certain groups, such as students or pensioners: a discount.

clue.text: Order cheap clothes child rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for child is read backwards

blocks.note: a kid is a child
tat is cheap, tasteless goods, such as shoddy clothes

explanation.surface: Someone orders cheap clothing that the child turns down.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consultation: an order.

clue.text: Condition that makes one restless?

blocks.note: surface reading: an illness causing fidgeting or agitation
setter's reading: rest-less, literally without rest, i.e. unable to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Restless' usually means fidgety; here it is taken literally as having no rest at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is a sleep disorder in which a person cannot get to sleep, so has no rest.

clue.text: Officer belonging to precinct protecting chief of police

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a member belongs in a group
a precinct is a district or sector
first letter of police

explanation.surface: A police officer at a precinct station guards the chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Chief of here means first letter, not a senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police officer ranking above a sergeant.

clue.text: China tea lab brewed is delicious

indicators.note: brewing mixes and stews ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: rhyming slang: china plate = mate, i.e. a pal
taken as written

explanation.surface: China tea brewed in a laboratory turns out tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the tea's origin, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable means pleasant to taste, so the near-synonym of delicious fits.

clue.text: Boring sample comprising carbon and rock

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A dull specimen made of carbon and rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but it means drilling: a sample taken by boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A core is a cylinder of rock or ice extracted by drilling, so a sample taken by boring.

clue.text: See report have an effect

blocks.note: first meaning: discern
a third meaning: to relate or inform
second meaning: to make an impact

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings strung together with no link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell is to discern something, and when strain or age tells it shows its impact.

clue.text: Rat's characteristic yellow pigment

blocks.note: a trait is a characteristic
or is the heraldic tincture gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A rat's distinctive yellow colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is': the rat is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in slang is a betrayer or informer, someone who turns on their own side.

clue.text: Taking on English politician making false claims about leader of opposition

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another
'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'opposition'

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Member of Parliament
making false statements
first letter of opposition

explanation.surface: An English MP is hiring staff while lying about the opposition leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on workers is to hire them, i.e. employ them.

clue.text: All excited about cold drink of milk

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
about means surrounding, so the stirred letters go round the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap
a common drink

explanation.surface: Everyone is thrilled about a cold drink of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink of milk' looks like one phrase; 'drink' gives TEA and only 'of milk' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal is an adjective meaning relating to or consisting of milk, from Latin lac.

clue.text: Person put forward new rule in overbearing manner after taking sides

indicators.note: taking the sides away strips off the outer letters at each end of the phrase's word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
to domineer is to rule arrogantly

explanation.surface: A candidate brings in a new rule, bossily, after choosing a side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking sides' suggests partisanship; here it means removing both end letters, D and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone proposed or put forward for an office or award.

clue.text: Go back on unrealistic promise we'd made ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
the last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Breaking an unrealistic promise that we made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back on' reads as one idiom; the definition is only 'Go back', and 'on' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw, as tide or a hairline does.

clue.text: Criticise article about temple

blocks.note: a critic pans a bad show
the definite article
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a piece written about a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a temple to all the gods; a pantheon is any such temple.

clue.text: File that may be used to support newspaper article

blocks.note: first meaning: a line of people one behind another

blocks.clueFragment: that may be used to support
blocks.note: a third meaning: a pillar holding up a roof
second meaning: a regular piece by a columnist

explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: a line of marchers, a supporting pillar, and a regular press piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers march in a column (a file), and a newspaper column is a regular feature.

clue.text: Start to learn every single actor's first name

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of learn
each means every one individually

explanation.surface: An actor learning each line starts with the first.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor is Cary Grant, 2 down, born Archibald Leach; 'first name' means his original surname, not a forename.
explanation.definitionFit: Cary Grant was born Archibald Alexander Leach, so Leach was the actor's original name.

clue.text: Impasse broken by British person working with me

indicators.note: a thing broken by something has that something forced into its middle

blocks.note: a stalemate is a deadlock
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A British colleague breaks a deadlock at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is someone from the same organisation or stable, a colleague working alongside you.

clue.text: Expert tackling new problem one may have to face

definitions.text: problem one may have to face

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, holding the other piece in its grip

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A specialist tackling a fresh difficulty they must confront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have to face' sounds like confronting a challenge; it means on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition that typically appears on the face, a literal problem to face.

clue.text: Joint bank statement revealing some doubts

blocks.note: a reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand in the sea
'er' is a hesitant sound expressing doubt

explanation.surface: A joint bank account statement showing some uncertainties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint bank statement' reads as a shared account, but joint is the definition and bank is a sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: Ambassador is partial to caramel cheesecake

indicators.note: partial means taking only a part, so the letters run inside the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An ambassador who has a fondness for caramel cheesecake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is partial to' looks like liking, but it means part of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Elchee is an old word, from Turkish, for an ambassador or envoy.
